title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: A rough, noisy audience recording that nonetheless captures a lively free concert with standout Good Lovin' and Lovelight moments.
ai_review.review: The show is remembered fondly as a free, hillside concert with an acoustic opening, NRPS set and solid Dead performances – especially Good Lovin', Lovelight, Hard To Handle and China/Rider. However, the audience‑taped source is plagued by heavy crowd noise and low fidelity, making many sections difficult to hear despite occasional clear spots.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the performance but consistently criticize the recording quality; averaging the mixed star ratings yields a mid‑range score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very noisy and muffled, with crowd din drowning the band for much of the set; occasional moments (e.g., Lovelight) are clearer but overall fidelity is low and far from soundboard quality.

show_quality.setlist_flow: An informal free concert with an acoustic Garcia/Weir opening, a New Riders set, and the Dead taking the stage amid political announcements; flow is uneven due to spoken interruptions but overall energetic.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned as part of the acoustic opening; no specific guitar commentary.
band_member_comments.Phil: Referenced only in the acoustic lineup (Lesh) without performance detail.
band_member_comments.Bob: Cited in the acoustic opening with Weir; no further remarks on his playing.
